doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

chapter: Denver youth and University of Denver
title: Deciding on music: high school band director and hockey pep band
summary: His clarinetist band director steered him to Denver with a scholarship and gave him gigs including the Dixieland pep band at hockey games.

bands.name: University of Denver Dixieland pep band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. Was there a particular point where you made the decision about music as your livelihood or did it just evolve, like this is an obvious thing for me?

It sort of evolved but around my junior year in high school I went to All-State band and my friends were there also, the seniors that were a year older than me. And yeah, they were going, being music majors, and they were going to the University of Denver and they were getting good scholarships and that’s because the band director had money to give. And he was also a clarinetist, and my last year or so in high school I studied with

him, and he also started giving me things that the college kids didn’t want to do. You know there was a little pep band, a Dixieland band that played for all the hockey games. And it was right above the net you know, one of the nets. And we played the fight song or whatever it was you know and we’d play a little bit before the thing started and we’d play during time outs and stuff like that. And so I had that as a gig. And it was, you know my band director gave to me, which was kind of cool. I was playing with college guys and I was playing clarinet in this group. And then he also, I ended up playing a show there once, you know, a Broadway show that they were staging. And so yeah, he was recruiting me that way and it was great you know. And so that’s why I went to school there. So I figured you know, music was the best thing I could do. Because I had no interest in anything else. And I didn’t work very hard at anything else. I just mainly practiced. And you know read about music and just sort of lived that kind of thing.
